claims.text: Peru’s presidency describes foundation, viceroyal residence and a specific palace-stall permission at Lima. Zagalsky distinguishes Potosí’s inspector and labour assignments from Toledo’s compulsory regional mita allocations. Specified quotas and theoretical rest did not make that labour voluntary. A shared viceroyal label cannot replace these different powers, and neither formal pay nor colonial foundation establishes consent or empty land.
